messages.subject: 2 small conferences in the Netherlands
messages.body_plain:
Apologies for cross-posting these announcements from Dr. Sara van Erp, but these small conferences might be of interest to anyone in/near Europe.
The first is an SEM conference in March, where Yves Rosseel will give a keynote, as will other members of the lavaan forum
The second is a Multilevel conference in April, where I will give a keynote and a workshop about MLSEM.
Please forward to any other colleagues you think would be interested.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

(1)

The conference Structural Equation Modeling: New Developments and Applications will be held on March 10-11, 2022 at Tilburg University in The Netherlands.

The goal of this conference is to bring together methodological and substantive researchers who work on or are interested in SEM.

Keynote speakers are: Prof. Dr. Yves Rosseel, Prof. Dr. Rogier Kievit, Dr. Suzanne Jak, Dr. Daniel Oberski, and Dr. Sara van Erp.

Abstract submission

Abstracts for a presentation should be submitted before January 7, 2022. Please email the abstract to: sem "at" tilburguniversity.edu <http://tilburguniversity.edu>. We will inform you whether your abstract has been accepted before February 1, 2022.

Pre- and post-conference workshops

There will be two pre-conference workshops on March 9th on Structural Equation Modeling with lavaan (by Prof. Dr. Yves Rosseel) and Bayesian Structural Equation Modeling (by Dr. Sara van Erp).

Costs

Attendance of the conference itself is free of charge. The registration fee to attend the pre-conference workshops, including lunch on Wednesday is 10 euros. If you wish to attend the conference dinner on Thursday, the fee equals 45 euros.

The conference website with further information and the registration form can be found here: https://www.tilburguniversity.edu/about/schools/socialsciences/organization/departments/methodology-statistics/events/structural-equation-modeling

Kind regards,

Sara van Erp (Utrecht University) and Joris Mulder (Tilburg University)

(2)

The 13th International Multilevel Conference will be held on April 12-13, 2022.

The conference will be about all aspects of statistical multilevel analysis: innovative applications, theory, software, and methodology. The conference will be in an informal style, with much room for discussion.

It will be held in the city centre of Utrecht, within a quarter hour walk or a five-minute bus ride from the Central railway station.

Invited speakers are Drs. George Leckie and Terrence D. Jorgensen.

Abstract submission

Deadlines for submitting an abstract: If you submit before the 1st of December (2021), you will be notified on the 15th of December if your abstract is accepted.

If you submit before 31st of January (2022), you will be notified on the 14th of February if your abstract is accepted.

This edition of the conference will also have the option for researchers working with empirical data to submit posters with questions about their analyses or sampling design.

During the conference you will have the opportunity to receive feedback on your (ongoing) research.

Young Researcher Award

The abstracts of four PhD students will be selected and these PhD students will be invited to present their work in a special symposium.

The best presentation will be awarded during the closing ceremony with the 'Best PhD Multilevel Presentation Award' and their conference fee will be reimbursed.

Pre- and post-conference workshops

There will be a pre- and/or post-conference workshop(s) on April 11th and 14th.

We are currently finalizing these workshops, workshop details will be updated on the conference website as soon as possible.

The conference website with further information on abstract submission can be found at http://multilevel.fss.uu.nl/

With kind regards,

Emmeke Aarts, Sara van Erp, Beth Grandfield and Mirjam Moerbeek

Utrecht University, The Netherlands

messages.subject: user-specified prior with argument target= "stanclassic" option
messages.subject_clean: user-specified prior with argument target= "stanclassic" option
messages.body_plain:
I need to change default prior when running a Bayesian SEM in blavaan (specifically speaking, I'd like to change the prior of regression parameter beta from normal distribution to Beta distribution). I'm hoping to stay away from having to specify each parameter separately with the prior() function, since our model is a bit complicated.

>From this link, http://ecmerkle.github.io/blavaan/articles/prior.html, it seems to be the key to opening up more flexibility in prior specification with argument target= "stanclassic" option, but it doesn't seem to work when we try including it in the syntax. We don't get an error message, but the model just won't fully run. We keep it going almost all day and still it doesn't give me any output. It's as if it kills the kernel.

I have searched for a solution for a long time but no finding. Any ideas for this would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Sixue

messages.subject: Re: user-specified prior with argument target= "stanclassic" option
messages.subject_clean: user-specified prior with argument target= "stanclassic" option
messages.body_plain:
Sixue

This example worked with the example from the bsem function, using the beta() for priors for regressions.
If you can share more details we can see where any specific error ir

library(blavaan)

?bsem

model <- '
  # latent variable definitions
     ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3
     dem60 =~ y1 + a*y2 + b*y3 + c*y4
     dem65 =~ y5 + a*y6 + b*y7 + c*y8

  # regressions
    dem60 ~ ind60
    dem65 ~ ind60 + dem60

  # residual correlations
    y1 ~~ y5
    y2 ~~ y4 + y6
    y3 ~~ y7
    y4 ~~ y8
    y6 ~~ y8
'

## unique priors for mv intercepts; parallel chains
fit <- bsem(model, data=PoliticalDemocracy, std.lv <http://std.lv>=T,
            dp=dpriors(beta="beta(1,1)"),
            target="stanclassic")
summary(fit)
